prompt: Say it politely, as a man: ___ jedno pivo. (I would like one beer.)
explanation: Chtěl bych + thing or verb is the polite 'I would like'. A woman says Chtěla bych. Plain Chci (I want) sounds blunt to staff.

prompt: Ask where it is: ___ nádraží? (Where is the station?)
explanation: Kde je + the place in its dictionary form. For plural things use Kde jsou: Kde jsou toalety?

prompt: Ask permission: ___ platit kartou? (Can I pay by card?)
explanation: Můžu + infinitive = can I / may I. Formal spelling: mohu. Můžeme = can we.

prompt: Ask a stranger for help: ___ mi pomoct? (Can you help me?)
explanation: Můžete + infinitive is the polite request to staff and strangers: Můžete mi to napsat? Even softer: Mohl byste…?

prompt: Ask staff whether they have it: ___ wifi? (Do you have wifi?)
explanation: Máte + thing asks any shop, hotel or restaurant: Máte volný stůl? Máte mapu? The answer is Máme (we have) or Nemáme.

prompt: Order it: Dám si ___. (I'll have the soup; soup = polévka)
explanation: Feminine nouns in -a switch to -u when they are the thing you want, order or look for: káva → kávu, voda → vodu, jízdenka → jízdenku.

prompt: Make it negative: mluvím česky (I speak Czech) → ___ česky
explanation: Stick ne- onto the front of the verb, as one word: nemám, nechci, nevím, nerozumím. 'Is not' is irregular: není.

prompt: Two of a neuter noun: ___ piva, prosím. (Two beers, please.)
explanation: Dva goes with masculine nouns (dva lístky, dva čaje); dvě with feminine and neuter nouns (dvě kávy, dvě piva).

prompt: Count five or more: pět ___ (five beers; beer = pivo)
explanation: 1 pivo, 2–4 piva, but from 5 up the noun goes into the genitive plural: pět piv, deset minut, sto korun, pět lístků.

prompt: To a town or into a place: do ___ (to the center; center = centrum)
explanation: do + genitive = to / into: do centra, do Prahy, do Brna, do hotelu, do muzea, do hospody.

prompt: Some places take a different 'to': Jedu ___ letiště. (I'm going to the airport.)
explanation: Use na, not do, with letiště, nádraží, náměstí, zastávka, Hrad, pošta, koncert, pivo: na nádraží, na Hrad, na pivo.

prompt: Say where you are: Jsem v ___. (I'm in Prague; Prague = Praha)
explanation: Being somewhere takes the locative: Praha → v Praze, Brno → v Brně, Krumlov → v Krumlově, hotel → v hotelu.

prompt: With something: káva s ___ (coffee with milk; milk = mléko)
explanation: s + instrumental: masculine and neuter nouns add -em (s mlékem, s knedlíkem, s ledem); feminine -a becomes -ou (se zmrzlinou).

prompt: Past tense, a man speaking: Včera ___ na Hradě. (Yesterday I was at the Castle.)
explanation: Past = the -l form + jsem, and jsem always sits in second place: Byl jsem tam. / Včera jsem tam byl. A woman says byla.

prompt: Talk about tomorrow: Zítra ___ v Brně. (Tomorrow I will be in Brno.)
explanation: Budu = I will be; budu + infinitive = I will do: budu čekat. Often the present plus zítra is enough: Zítra jedu do Brna.
